item.title: Schema Exploitation Jailbreak
item.description:
Date: 10/31/2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Prompt Engineering", "Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities"]
Summary:
  • Large Language Models follow structured data schemas closely.
  • This behavior creates a security vulnerability.
  • The BreakFun attack exploits this with multi-part prompts.
  • It uses a Trojan Schema to embed harmful requests.
  • The attack misdirects the model's cognitive processing.
  • This bypasses existing safety mechanisms.

item.title: Persuasive Jailbreak Fingerprint
item.description:
Date: October 1, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence Security", "Natural Language Processing", "Machine Learning Vulnerabilities", "Social Engineering", "Ethical AI"]
Summary:
  • Large Language Models are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks using persuasion.
  • Attackers use Cialdini's seven persuasion principles to reframe harmful prompts.
  • These prompts bypass safety filters and remain human-readable.
  • The attack varies by principle and model, showing unique persuasive fingerprints.
  • It affects many popular LLMs like Vicuna and Llama.
  • The technique is stealthy and hard to detect automatically.

item.title: Pattern Enhanced Multi-Turn Jailbreaking
item.description:
Date: October 1, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Model Vulnerabilities", "Prompt Engineering", "Cybersecurity"]
Summary:
  • The article discusses multi-turn jailbreaking in large language models.
  • It reveals structural vulnerabilities in popular AI models.
  • Several models like GPT-4o-mini and llama3-8b are affected.
  • The research highlights pattern-based exploitation techniques.
  • This work aims to improve AI security and robustness.

item.title: Distributed Backdoor in Multi-Agent Systems
item.description:
Date: October 1, 2025
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Multi-Agent Systems", "Backdoor Attacks", "Large Language Models", "Software Vulnerabilities"]
Summary:
  • A distributed backdoor named Collaborative Shadows targets multi-agent systems.
  • Attackers embed encrypted attack primitives in multiple agent tools.
  • A crafted user instruction triggers and decrypts these primitives.
  • Agents collaborate in sequence to release the payload fragments.
  • The full malicious payload is reassembled post-task to exfiltrate data.
  • The backdoor evades detection by inspecting agents individually.
